text: The pulp editors wanted adventure, and I had lived some. Most fellows writing about cavalry charges had never sat on a horse.

choices.text: Which magazines did you write for?

text: Adventure and Argosy, mostly. Soldiering yarns and history, the kind of thing a boy reads under the covers with a flashlight.

choices.text: Had you written anything before the pulps?

text: A book, Modern Cavalry, published by Macmillan in 1922. Serious stuff for serious officers. The pulps paid better than military theory, I'll say that.

choices.text: How much did the pulps pay?

text: A penny or two a word. You learn to make every word earn its keep.

choices.text: Did you do anything besides magazines?

text: In 1925 I started my own outfit to sell my work to the newspapers. We even ran Treasure Island as a comic strip.

choices.text: Is that how you got into comics?
